BiblicalUsage: Chadel means frail, forsaken, ceasing. The psalmist asks to know his end, that he may know how frail he is; Isaiah's Servant is despised and rejected of men; and Ezekiel is told that he who forbears may forbear, and he who hears may hear.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe frailty and rejection meet in one Man: the Servant was despised and rejected, and the psalmist's frailty is the reason He came. God does not despise the frail — He became forsaken for them.
